propositions.text: The claimants are a family of three Mexican citizens seeking refugee protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(b).
propositions.quote: XXX XXXXX XXXXX, 32 years old, his spouse XXXX XXXX XXXXX XXXX, 26 years old, and their daughter XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX, five years old, all Mexican citizens, are claiming refugee protection in Canada under section 96 and paragraph 97(1)(b) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimants are a Mexican family seeking refugee protection in Canada under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1)(b).

propositions.text: The male claimant is the designated representative of his minor daughter.
propositions.quote: XXX XXXXX XXXXX is his minor daughter's designated representative.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the male claimant is his minor daughter's designated representative.

propositions.text: The female claimant alleged she found torn ballots during the 2007 municipal elections and discussed them with her spouse and his brother.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX alleged that on XXXXX, 2007, during the municipal elections, she found a number of torn ballots in a plastic bag. She brought the bag home and talked about it with her spouse, XXX, and his brother.

propositions.text: They suggested taking the torn ballots to the municipal president, XXXXX XXXXX.
propositions.quote: They suggested to her that the ballots be taken to the municipal president, XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the female claimant found torn ballots in 2007 and was advised to take them to the municipal president.

propositions.text: Mr. XXXXX became aggressive upon seeing the torn ballots and threatened to kill them if he had difficulties.
propositions.quote: Mr. XXXXX became very aggressive when he saw the torn ballots and asked her not to talk about it and threatened to kill them if he had difficulties.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports Mr. XXXXX reacted aggressively and threatened them over the torn ballots.

propositions.text: Six weeks later, the claimants decided to report and saw the PRD municipal candidate, who said he could not do much.
propositions.quote: Six weeks later, the claimants decided that it was their duty to report, and they went to see the PRD (party of the democratic revolution) municipal candidate, XXXXX XXXXX, who told them that he could not do much.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants waited six weeks before reporting to the PRD candidate, who said he could not help.

propositions.text: AFI officers came to question the female claimant on behalf of Mr. XXXXX in 2007.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX, 2007, some AFI officers came to ask her questions, specifying that they came on behalf of Mr. XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports AFI officers questioned the female claimant on Mr. XXXXX's behalf in 2007.

propositions.text: The claimants participated in demonstrations against electoral fraud in 2008.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX and on XXXXX, 2008, the claimants participated in a demonstration against electoral fraud.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants participated in anti-electoral fraud demonstrations in 2008.

propositions.text: In 2008, the female claimant and the principal claimant's brother were forced into a bus and beaten; the principal claimant was also beaten at home by AFI officers.
propositions.quote: On XXXXX, 2008, XXXX XXXX and the principal claimant's brother were forced to climb in a bus, and they were beaten. The claimants participated in another demonstration on XXXXX, 2008, and the AFI police officers came to their home and beat the principal claimant, who was alone at home.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants were beaten by AFI officers in 2008 during and after demonstrations.

propositions.text: The claimants left home to stay with the male claimant's sister until 2008 when they saw AFI officers who had attacked them.
propositions.quote: The claimants decided then to leave their home and stayed at the male claimant's sister's home, where they remained until XXXXX, 2008, when they saw the AFI officers' van pass by carrying the officers who had attacked them.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants stayed with the male claimant's sister until 2008 when they saw the AFI officers who attacked them.

propositions.text: Their hosts asked them to leave; they returned home but AFI officers tried to break in, and the principal claimant escaped and got help from bystanders who scared the officers away.
propositions.quote: Their hosts asked them to leave, and they returned home, but on XXXXX, 2008, the AFI squadron returned to their home and tried to break open their door. The principal claimant exited through the back door and asked for help from people who were playing baseball in a park. These people made the AFI officers flee by yelling at them to leave.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants were forced to leave, AFI officers tried to break in, but bystanders scared them off.

propositions.text: The claimants decided to leave Mexico and arrived in Montréal in 2008.
propositions.quote: They decided then to leave Mexico and arrived in Montréal on XXXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker reports the claimants left Mexico and arrived in Montréal in 2008.

propositions.text: The claimants' identity was satisfactorily established through their passports seized by Immigration Canada.
propositions.quote: The claimants' identity was established in a satisfactory manner through their passport, seized by Immigration Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants' identity was satisfactorily established through passports seized by Immigration Canada.

propositions.text: The claimants' testimony was unclear, imprecise, and contained implausibilities, contradictions, and omissions affecting credibility.
propositions.quote: The claimants' testimony was not clear or precise and contained implausibilities, contradictions and omissions that altered the credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants' testimony unclear and containing contradictions and omissions that affect credibility.

propositions.text: The principal claimant fears Mr. XXXXX and said problems began in 2007 when she took him damaged ballot boxes found on election day.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant testified that she fears XXXXX XXXXX, former municipal president, and specified that her problems began on XXXXX, 2007, when she took him the damaged ballot boxes that she had found in the building hallways on election day.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant fears Mr. XXXXX and said problems began in 2007 when she took him damaged ballots.

propositions.text: She said she brought the ballots home and was advised by husband and brother-in-law to take them to the mayor.
propositions.quote: She testified that she allegedly brought the ballots home and that it was her husband and her brother-in-law who allegedly advised her to take them to the mayor.

propositions.text: When asked why she did not return ballots to election authorities that day, she said she thought about calling someone with more power and was told to take them to the mayor, a PAN member.
propositions.quote: When asked why she had not returned them to the election authorities that day, she responded that she had thought about calling someone who had more power and that, when she talked to her brother-in-law, he had told her to take them to the mayor and specified that the mayor is a member of the National Action Party (PAN).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant said she was advised to take ballots to the mayor, a PAN member, instead of election authorities.

propositions.text: She did not know how many ballots were in the boxes and said the mayor threatened them when they met him; six weeks later they decided to report him.
propositions.quote: When she was asked how many ballots were in the boxes, she responded that she did not know and then continued by saying that when her brother, spouse and she met the mayor, he threatened them, and six weeks later, they decided to report him.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant did not know the number of ballots and said the mayor threatened them; they reported him six weeks later.

propositions.text: She said election results had been announced when they decided to report the mayor, and a PRD candidate had been elected.
propositions.quote: When asked to explain whether the election results had been announced when they decided to report Mr. XXXXX, she responded that they had and specified that it was a candidate from the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), XXXXX XXXXX, who had been elected.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant said election results were announced and a PRD candidate was elected when they reported the mayor.

propositions.text: The principal claimant said the mayor became angry; she was disappointed he did not act and said the mayor told XXXXX XXXXX she had come to see him.
propositions.quote: The principal claimant stated that when she met Mr. XXXXX, he became angry. When asked to explain why in her story she stated that she was disappointed by Mr. XXXXX's reaction, the female claimant responded: [translation] "I was thinking that he could do something". She testified that it was Mr. XXXXX who allegedly told XXXXX XXXXX that she had come to see him.

propositions.text: When asked why a PRD member who won the election would report them to the mayor, she said she did not know.
propositions.quote: When asked why Mr. XXXXX, who is a PRD member and who won the elections, would allegedly report them to Mr. XXXXX, the female claimant responded: [translation] "I don't know".

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant said the mayor was angry, she was disappointed, and did not know why a PRD member would report them to the mayor.

propositions.text: The principal claimant said she voted for the PRD but reported torn ballots to the outgoing PAN mayor, saying she was not politically oriented and did not connect party and fraud.
propositions.quote: In addition, when asked what party she voted for, she responded that she voted for the PRD; when asked to explain why, if she voted for the PRD she reported the torn ballots to the mayor, the outgoing PAN member, the female claimant responded that she had not made the connection between the political party and the fraud, and she specified that she was not politically oriented.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the principal claimant voted for PRD but reported torn ballots to PAN mayor, saying she was not politically oriented.

propositions.text: The panel finds it surprising that fraudsters left torn ballots and that claimants waited six weeks to report the mayor after elections ended and he lost.
propositions.quote: The panel is surprised on the one hand that the fraudsters were negligent enough to leave the torn ballots; it also finds it surprising that the claimants waited six weeks to report the mayor when the elections had finished and he had not won.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it surprising that torn ballots were left and the claimants waited six weeks to report the mayor after elections ended and he lost.

propositions.text: The claimants' suggestion of complicity between the outgoing mayor and opposing party member is implausible
propositions.quote: the most implausible part of this story is that the claimants suggested that there was some complicity between the outgoing mayor, Mr. XXXXX, and Mr. XXXXX, of the opposing party.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the claimants' suggestion of complicity between the outgoing mayor and opposing party member implausible.

propositions.text: It is implausible that Mr. XXXXX of the PRD would report people who informed him of fraud of which he was a victim
propositions.quote: it is implausible that Mr. XXXXX, who is of the PRD, would have reported the people who allegedly informed him of the fraud, of which he was allegedly a victim.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it implausible that Mr. XXXXX of the PRD would report informants of fraud against him.

propositions.text: Claimants alleged participation in several demonstrations against election fraud in 2007 and 2008 organized by PRD members
propositions.quote: the claimants alleged that they participated in several demonstrations against election fraud, on XXXXX, 2007, and XXXXX and XX, 2008, organized by some PRD members against the irregularity in the elections.

paragraphs.summary: The claimants allege they participated in demonstrations against election fraud organized by PRD members in 2007 and 2008.

propositions.text: AFI officers allegedly arrested and beat claimants after 2008 demonstrations and searched the principal claimant's home for ballots
propositions.quote: some AFI officers allegedly arrested and beat Messrs. XXX and XXXXX XXXX XXXX and, after the XXXXX, 2008, demonstration, the AFI officers came to their home and allegedly hit the principal claimant and searched the house for the ballots.

paragraphs.summary: The claimants allege AFI officers arrested, beat them, and searched their home for ballots after 2008 demonstrations.

propositions.text: Principal claimant said Mr. XXXXX sent officers to search her house for more ballots
propositions.quote: When asked to explain who was sending the officers, the principal claimant responded that it was Mr. XXXXX, and when asked why the officers were searching her house looking for the ballots, seeing that she had returned them to him, she responded: "He thought that there were more".

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant said Mr. XXXXX sent officers to search her house for more ballots.

propositions.text: Panel draws negative inference from discrepancy in female claimant's testimony about officers breaking door and her location
propositions.quote: the panel draws a negative inference from the fact that the immigration officer's notes from the interview with the female claimant state: "on XXXXX, 2008, the officers came again and broke down the door. I went to find help in a baseball park"; however, in her PIF, she alleged that this incident happened on XXXXX and that, on XXXXX, she was at her sister-in-law's home in Mexico City.

paragraphs.summary: The court draws a negative inference from the female claimant's contradictory testimony about officers breaking her door and her whereabouts.

propositions.text: The story is not credible
propositions.quote: The panel finds that this story is not credible;

propositions.text: Even if credible, a reasonable internal flight alternative exists
propositions.quote: however, even if it were, there would be a reasonable internal flight alternative in this case.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the story not credible but says even if it were, a reasonable internal flight alternative exists.

propositions.text: Claimants testified they stayed with sister in Mexico City but saw AFI officers in a van and returned to mother's home
propositions.quote: The claimants testified that they went to stay with their sister in Mexico City but believe that they were found there because while they were returning from shopping, and they were in their car, they allegedly saw a van carrying the same AFI officers who had come to their home in XXXXX; they testified that they allegedly lost them and that they returned to their mother's home.

paragraphs.summary: The claimants testified they stayed with their sister in Mexico City but saw AFI officers and returned to their mother's home.

propositions.text: Panel believes principal claimant adjusted testimony and claimants did not prove AFI officers found them in Mexico City
propositions.quote: The panel is of the opinion that it is an adjustment in her testimony and that the claimants did not demonstrate that they had been found in Mexico City by the AFI officers, who never went to their sister's home.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the principal claimant adjusted testimony and claimants did not prove AFI officers found them in Mexico City.

propositions.text: Principal claimant said settling in Mexico City or Guadalajara is impossible because they would be found via elector's card
propositions.quote: When asked to consider the possibility of settling in Mexico City or in Guadalajara, the principal claimant responded that she does not think it is possible because they will find them with the help of their elector's card.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant said settling in Mexico City or Guadalajara is impossible due to risk of being found via elector's card.

propositions.text: Principal claimant said AFI officers recently searched mother's home and adjusted testimony about their surveillance
propositions.quote: the AFI police officers recently went to her mother's home looking for her. Asked to explain why they waited two and a half years to go to her mother's home, she adjusted her testimony and stated that during that period, she would see them pass in front of her home, which was still being watched.

paragraphs.summary: The principal claimant said AFI officers recently searched mother's home and adjusted testimony about ongoing surveillance.

propositions.text: This omission undermines the female claimant's credibility
propositions.quote: This is a significant omission that undermines the female claimant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the female claimant's omission significantly undermines her credibility.

propositions.text: Male claimant said his brother returned to Mexico, lives quietly since 2010, and has no problems
propositions.quote: the male claimant responded that he returned to Mexico and that he lives in XXXXX. When asked whether his brother has problems, he responded that he does not and explained that he has been living there quietly since XXXXX 2010.

paragraphs.summary: The male claimant said his brother returned to Mexico, lives quietly since 2010, and has no problems.

propositions.text: Claimants did not discharge burden of proof and did not show internal flight alternative does not exist
propositions.quote: The claimants did not discharge their burden of proof and did not show that an IFA does not exist.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes claimants failed to prove that an internal flight alternative does not exist.

propositions.text: Claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection
propositions.quote: the panel determines that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" or "persons in need of protection".

paragraphs.summary: The court determines the claimants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection.

propositions.text: The panel rejects the refugee protection claim of the named claimants
propositions.quote: The panel rejects the refugee protection claim of XXX XXXXX XXXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXXX XXXX and XXXXX XXXXX XXXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The court rejects the refugee protection claim of the named claimants.
